title: Fynaptix · Defense Tech Research
heading: Defense Technology Intelligence
subheading: AI battlefield software, drones, autonomy & European rearmament
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Defense names carry policy, program-concentration, and valuation risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: EU defence spending is projected to hit €454B in 2026 (2.4% of GDP), after €418B/2.2% GDP in 2025, inside a newly finalized EU Council-Parliament 'ReArm Europe' framework targeting €800B in defence investment by 2030; 23 of 27 EU states already met the 2% NATO benchmark in 2025, with Estonia and Lithuania projected above 5% of GDP in 2026

kpis.sub: Q1 2026 · DEFENSE TECH VC, ALREADY TOPS ALL OF 2025's $9.6B
kpis.label: 262 deals in Q1 alone with early-stage rounds pricing at 17-50x revenue; Anduril's targeted $100B round, first reported Jul 24, remains unclosed seven weeks later as of Sep 7 — CEO Brian Schimpf has now confirmed the company is delaying its own IPO, calling it "bad" to list "in the middle of a hype cycle" — while hypersonic-missile startup Castelion pulled in the week's largest fresh VC round

Defense Autonomous Warfare Group request inside a record $75B FY27 drone/counter-drone budget ask ($13.4B total autonomy request); the Sep 1 continuing resolution funds government through Dec 11 at FY26 levels but leaves FY27 appropriations, the CCA Increment 2 downselect, and Golden Dome's reconciliation-dependent funding all unresolved — Golden Dome lead Gen. Guetlein warned Aug 12 the program itself is at risk without a fiscal 2026 topline to fall back on

Section 232 tariffs (25% on smaller drones/components, up to 100% on units >25kg or with thermal imaging) took effect Sep 3, with UK-origin goods getting a preferential 10% rate versus 15% for EU, Japan, Switzerland, Taiwan, South Korea and Liechtenstein; RCAT, ONDS, AVAV, KTOS and UMAC all rose on the news, reinforcing AeroVironment's own Sep 2 first-ever US military directed-energy production award as a domestic-manufacturing tailwind

tiers.label: Established / Software & Primes
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: The Army moved TITAN into production Sep 1-2 with a $192M order split $127M to Palantir and $65M to Anduril for eight ground-station systems over 18 months, and shares closed at $174.48 (Sep 4, down from $186.29 on Aug 28) on a ~150x trailing P/E after whipsawing between a 6% Sep 2 drop and a 7.8% Sep 3 pop on an expanded PwC AI partnership
rows.watch for: Michael Burry renewed his bear case Sep 2, putting a number on it — Palantir's ~$432B market cap could eventually fall below $100B — citing a ~32% deferred-revenue ratio nearly matching consulting peer Accenture's and $265M of Q2 stock-based comp; single-day 6-8% swings on non-fundamental news show how sentiment-driven the stock remains

rows.angle: Q2's book-to-bill ratio topped 3x on €11.4B of new order nominations (+~500% YoY), and the company is committing ~€270M to a new Kassel hub (drone test centre, expanded tank plant to 3,500 workers, logistics/training centre by end-2027) plus a fresh air-defence milestone with Hensoldt at the Timber Express 2026 exercise; shares nonetheless drifted to ~€1,034, still absorbing the post-F126 guidance cut
rows.watch for: Record order intake still isn't showing up in the share price; the Lockheed ATACMS joint-production line won't generate revenue until 2028

rows.angle: Shares closed near $256.65 (Sep 4, down from $263.56) on a $41B backlog and a fresh $1B missile-production investment; Jefferies reiterated Hold with a $315 target (Aug 26), and successor CEO Sam Mehta has offered no further detail nearly three weeks after Chris Kubasik's ouster
rows.watch for: Golden Dome's own FY27 funding was flagged as being at risk by program lead Gen. Guetlein on Aug 12, since it leans on reconciliation funding with no FY26 topline to fall back on if that stalls — a direct read-through to L3Harris's satellite and interceptor work

rows.angle: H1 2026 sales +9% to £15.8B on £16.4B of H1 orders, with management's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, 10-12% EBIT growth, >£2B free cash flow) unchallenged by any negative news this period; shares closed at 1,979p (Sep 4, -0.43%), still sidestepping the small-cap drone and PLTR volatility hitting US peers
rows.watch for: H2 follow-through on the newly raised guidance is the next real test

tiers.label: High-Growth Autonomy Pure-Plays
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: The Sep 2 $464.8M directed-energy award (LOCUST X3 lasers for the Army's Enduring-High Energy Laser program) is real revenue diversification beyond drones, but it landed against a harder backdrop: a January stop-work order on the SCAR/BADGER satellite-antenna program drove a $151.3M goodwill impairment, an error in that impairment calculation then forced a restatement understating net loss by $87.3M, and securities-fraud class actions are now proceeding; shares closed at $144.65 (Sep 4, -1.74%), down roughly 40%+ YTD
rows.watch for: Sep 9 earnings (consensus $0.34 EPS, $474.6M revenue) carries an options-implied 13% move — the first real test of whether the laser win or the accounting overhang dominates investor reaction

rows.angle: Shares steadied further in the ~$47-49 range, with Kratos folding its Skyborg-era XQ-58 Valkyrie work into a CCA Increment 2 pitch and landing a new Marine Corps MUX TACAIR award alongside Northrop Grumman; analyst views remain split — Truist cut its target to $104 from $135 (Buy) while Raymond James raised its target to $80 from $40 (Strong Buy)
rows.watch for: Still absorbing dilution from the Aug 14 $1.4B follow-on offering; remains excluded from the June CCA Increment 1 production award (Anduril & General Atomics)

rows.angle: Shares closed near $8.36 (Sep 4) as the company's Blue Ops maritime division struck a tie-up with Havoc to integrate collaborative-autonomy and command software across its uncrewed surface vessels, and closed the Apium Swarm Robotics acquisition to add multi-agent swarm autonomy — building on last quarter's 527% YoY revenue growth to $20.2M and $325M of cash on hand
rows.watch for: Whether the maritime and swarm-autonomy pushes convert into contracted revenue; the stock is a direct beneficiary of the new Section 232 drone tariffs as a US-based maker

rows.angle: Shares held near $7.62, still down roughly 20%+ YTD, with no fresh company-specific catalyst this period beyond the broader drone-tariff tailwind that lifted the whole small-cap group
rows.watch for: Needs an operational catalyst to move independent of the broader small-cap drone complex; margin and profitability visibility still unproven

private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: Talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed seven weeks later, as of Sep 7 — more than 3x the $30.5B mark from just over a year ago and up from the $61B May 2026 round (Thrive Capital, a16z). CEO Brian Schimpf has now confirmed the company is delaying its own IPO, calling it "bad" to list "in the middle of a hype cycle," even while pursuing this raise; the Sep 1-2 $65M TITAN production order and June's FQ-44A CCA award keep revenue scaling in the meantime.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the ~$1.5B round (Mar 2026) that valued the company at $12.7B, co-led by Advent International and JPMorgan's Security & Resiliency Initiative. Continuing to compete for the Navy's up-to-$800M ISR task-order pool using the V-BAT drone, and Poland's Ministry of National Defence has now awarded Shield AI a V-BAT contract, making Poland the first NATO eastern-flank nation to deploy the platform.

private_watchlist.name: Saronic
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; continuing to scale its NVIDIA-powered autonomy stack and its Franklin, Louisiana shipyard (part of a $300M expansion) toward a stated target of 20+ autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027. Still marked by the $1.75B Series D led by Kleiner Perkins.

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.8B Series E closed Jul 13, 2026 (Lightspeed, General Catalyst, JPMorgan, Iconiq) — the largest defence-tech round in European history. Continues fielding the HX-2 strike drone in Ukraine and building out its Altra battle-management software and CA-1 Europa uncrewed-fighter concept.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations still elevated
bear_case.description: Michael Burry renewed his Palantir warning Sep 2, arguing the company behaves more like a consulting business than software and that its ~$432B market cap could eventually fall below $100B, citing a ~32% deferred-revenue ratio nearly matching Accenture's and $265M of Q2 stock-based comp — shares still rebounded 7.8% the next day on unrelated PwC partnership news, showing how sentiment-driven the stock remains.

bear_case.title: AeroVironment's restatement is a live example of defense-tech execution risk
bear_case.description: A January stop-work order on the SCAR/BADGER satellite-antenna program triggered a $151.3M goodwill impairment; an error in that calculation then forced AeroVironment to restate financials, understating its nine-month net loss by $87.3M, and securities-fraud class actions are now proceeding into Sep 9 earnings — a reminder that fast-growing defense-tech names can carry real accounting and disclosure risk alongside the growth story.

bear_case.title: The defense-tech VC boom still looks like a bubble
bear_case.description: Anduril's targeted $100B round remains unclosed seven weeks after first being reported, and CEO Brian Schimpf has now confirmed the company is delaying its own IPO because it's "bad" to list "in the middle of a hype cycle" — even as hypersonic-missile startup Castelion pulled in the week's largest fresh VC round, showing capital is still chasing the space at a pace some insiders themselves call unsustainable.

bear_case.title: The Sep 1 stopgap and Golden Dome's funding fragility just push the fight to December
bear_case.description: The continuing resolution funds government (and defense) through Dec 11 at FY26 levels but settles nothing on FY27 appropriations, the $54.6B DAWG autonomy line item, or the CCA Increment 2 downselect; Golden Dome's own lead, Gen. Guetlein, warned Aug 12 that the missile-shield program is at risk because it depends on reconciliation funding with no FY26 topline behind it if that process stalls.

bear_case.title: Governance and program-execution risk hits even established primes
bear_case.description: Nearly three weeks after L3Harris ousted CEO Chris Kubasik with no further explanation offered, the uncertainty remains unresolved, and Rheinmetall's F126 frigate cancellation is still weighing on shares (down to ~€1,034 despite a record Q2 book-to-bill and fresh Kassel-hub and Hensoldt news) — proof that record backlogs don't insulate a prime from sudden leadership or program shocks.

catalysts.title: Rheinmetall commits ~€270M to Kassel defense hub
catalysts.description: New drone test centre, an expanded tank plant (workforce to 3,500) and a logistics/training centre due live by end-2027, even as shares drift to ~€1,034, still absorbing the post-F126 guidance cut.

catalysts.title: Army awards $192M to Palantir and Anduril as TITAN moves to production
catalysts.description: Eight initial ground-station systems split between the two companies ($127M Palantir, $65M Anduril) with delivery over the next 18 months.

catalysts.title: AeroVironment wins first-ever US military directed-energy production contract
catalysts.description: $464.8M award for LOCUST X3 30kW laser systems under the Army's Enduring-High Energy Laser program, diversifying AVAV's revenue beyond drones ahead of Sep 9 earnings.

catalysts.title: Michael Burry renews Palantir bear case; PwC partnership drives Sep 3 rebound
catalysts.description: Burry warned Palantir's ~$432B market cap could eventually fall below $100B; shares fell 6% on the post before jumping 7.8% the next day on an expanded PwC AI partnership.

catalysts.title: House passes stopgap funding bill, averting a shutdown
catalysts.description: Passed 370-48; funds government including defense through Dec 11 at FY26 levels, pushing the FY27 appropriations fight — and the CCA Increment 2 downselect — past the November midterms.

etfs.name: Global X Defense Tech
etfs.summary: Tilted toward Palantir and autonomy pure-plays, with almost 38% annualized returns since its Sept 2023 inception; this week's PLTR whipsaws and AVAV's accounting overhang make for a choppier short-term read than the cap-weighted primes indices, even as the long-run trend holds

etfs.name: iShares US Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: Largest in category at ~$13.3B AUM; broad US primes exposure has stayed largely insulated from this week's small-cap drone, PLTR and AVAV volatility; 0.38% expense ratio

etfs.name: Invesco Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: ~11% YTD in 2026, ~29% over the trailing year; US-focused, adds commercial aerospace (Boeing, GE Aerospace, RTX); trades at a lower P/E (~27x) than ITA (~31x)

etfs.name: Select STOXX Europe Defense
etfs.summary: European names continue absorbing Rheinmetall's F126-driven share drift even as record Q2 order intake (3x book-to-bill, €11.4B of nominations) and fresh wins (Kassel hub, Hensoldt milestone) keep backlogs growing, against a newly finalized €800B 'ReArm Europe' spending framework through 2030

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: H1 2026 sales +9% to £15.8B on £16.4B of orders, with management's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, >£2B free cash flow) unchallenged by any negative news this period and shares continuing to sidestep the small-cap drone and PLTR/AVAV volatility hitting US peers — the most straightforward name to hold, UK-listed with no wrapper needed.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Analyst views stayed split this week (Truist cut to $104, Raymond James raised to $80) while Kratos folds its Skyborg-era XQ-58 Valkyrie work into a CCA Increment 2 pitch and lands a new Marine Corps MUX TACAIR award with Northrop Grumman, but the stock is still absorbing August's $1.4B dilutive follow-on and remains excluded from the June CCA Increment 1 win — real optionality, real price risk, small size only. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: 527% YoY revenue growth to $20.2M, $325M of cash, and this week's Blue Ops/Havoc maritime-autonomy tie-up plus the closed Apium Swarm Robotics acquisition mark a genuine shift from single-drone vendor toward a backlog-driven autonomy platform — upgrading off Avoid, though the story is still young enough that this stays speculative, small size only. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: The Sep 2 $464.8M laser contract is real diversification, but it can't offset the SCAR/BADGER stop-work-driven goodwill impairment, the resulting restatement that understated nine-month net loss by $87.3M, and the securities-fraud class actions now heading into Sep 9 earnings — downgrading off Speculative until that overhang clears. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Golden Dome lead Gen. Guetlein warned Aug 12 that the program's reconciliation-dependent FY27 funding is at risk, and Jefferies' Aug 26 Hold sits atop an unexplained CEO ouster now three weeks old — real backlog strength (a fresh $1B missile-production investment) still can't outweigh two unresolved overhangs. Also sits in the Space sleeve via satellite work — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: A >3x book-to-bill ratio on €11.4B of Q2 order nominations (+~500% YoY) plus a new Hensoldt-partnered air-defence milestone and the €270M Kassel-hub commitment haven't stopped shares drifting to ~€1,034, still absorbing the F126 guidance cut — record order intake isn't showing up in the price yet, so this stays a watch; directly accessible from the UK without a US wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Burry's Sep 2 renewed critique put a specific number on the bear case — a ~$432B market cap that could fall below $100B — even as the Sep 1-2 $192M Army TITAN production award proves the government business keeps growing; ~150x trailing earnings is still too rich to hold here. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Shares held near $7.62, still down roughly 20%+ YTD with no fresh company-specific catalyst this period beyond the broader drone-tariff tailwind — margin and profitability visibility remains the gating issue keeping this off Core.
